## Workshop aims

Participants ...

-   understand how [`propop`](https://statistik-aargau.github.io/propop/) implements the cohort component method.
-   can run a population projection with [`propop::propop()`](https://github.com/statistik-aargau/propop/blob/main/R/propop.R).
-   *optional: can prepare their own data for [`propop::propop()`](https://github.com/statistik-aargau/propop/blob/main/R/propop.R).*
-   *optional: know how to prepare and run projections for subregions.*
-   *optional: can evaluate, visualize and interpret the results.*

\

# The cohort component method

## The cohort component method

::: {style="font-size: 95%;"}
Population $+$ [births]{style="color: #007AB8;"} $-$ [deaths]{style="color: #007AB8;"} $+$ [immigration]{style="color: #007AB8;"} $-$ [emigration]{style="color: #007AB8;"} $=$ new population

[{{< fa person size=2x >}} {{< fa person-dress size=3x >}}]{style="color: #333333;"} [{{< fa plus >}} {{< fa baby size=3x >}} {{< fa minus >}} {{< fa cross size=3x >}} {{< fa plus >}} {{< fa plane-arrival size=3x >}} {{< fa minus >}} {{< fa plane-departure size=3x >}} {{< fa equals >}}]{style="color: #007AB8;"} [{{< fa person size=2x >}} {{< fa person-dress size=3x >}} {{< fa person size=3x >}}]{style="color: #333333;"}

\

:::{ .fragment}
-   Starting point: observed population by age and sex (optional: nationality).
-   Each cohort is carried forward year by year.
-   Assumptions about [**components**]{style="color: #007AB8;"} contain social, political and economic trends.
:::
:::

::: {.absolute bottom="20px" left="0px" style="font-size: 18px;"}
Preston, Guillot, and Heuveline (2000); Statistik Aargau (2025); Bundesamt für Statistik BFS (2025)
:::

## Cohort component method in `propop`

Typically **404 demographic groups**:\
2 nationalities × 2 sexes × 101 ages (0 to 100+)

::: {.fragment}
-   Acquisition of the Swiss citizenship: people move from the non-Swiss to the Swiss groups.
-   Without nationality distinction: 202 groups.
:::

\

::: {.fragment}
[**Questions to the room:**]{style="color: #007AB8;"}\

-   [Who of you distinguishes between nationalities for their projection?]{style="color: #007AB8;"}\
-   [Who of your uses another number of age groups for the projection?]{style="color: #007AB8;"}
:::

## The FSO equation: cohort transition

::: {style="font-size: 95%;"}
$$
P_{n,i} = \underbrace{P_{n-1,i-1}}_{\text{Starting population}} \times
\underbrace{\left[(1-q^p_{n,i}) - (e_{n,i} + \varepsilon_{n,i} + a_{n,i})\left(1-\tfrac{q^p_{n,i}}{2}\right)\right]}_{\text{Rates: mortality, emigration*, citizenship acquisition}}
$$

-   **Rates** determine how many people reach the next age ($i$) cohort per year ($n$).
-   Emigrants are exposed to half a year of mortality: factor $(1 - q/2)$.
-   *emigration rates:\
    -   $e$ = international emigration\
    -   $\varepsilon$ = intercantonal emigration

:::

::: {.absolute bottom="20px" left="0px" style="font-size: 18px;"}
Office fédéral de la statistique (2020). [*Méthodes pour les scénarios cantonaux*](https://github.com/statistik-aargau/propop-additional-resources/blob/358ffa280f3777af34d3ac4b2782c1171ed93beb/FSO_2020_Meth_scenarios%20cant.pdf)
:::

## The FSO equation: adding newcomers

::: {style="font-size: 95%;"}
$$
P_{n,i} = P_{n-1,i-1} \times \left[\dots\right] +
\underbrace{(I^E_{n,i} + I^I_{n,i} + A_{n,i})\left(1-\tfrac{q^p_{n,i}}{2}\right)}_{\text{Absolute numbers: immigration, citizenship acquisition}}
$$

-   **Absolute numbers** for immigration add new people.
-   **Births** are not shown in this equation (see [`calculate_newborns()`](https://github.com/statistik-aargau/propop/blob/main/R/calculate_newborns.R))).
-   Immigrants are exposed to half a year of mortality: factor $(1 - q/2)$.
-   *immigration numbers:\
    -   $I^E$ = international immigration\
    -   $I^I$ = intercantonal immigration
    
:::

::: {.absolute bottom="20px" left="0px" style="font-size: 18px;"}
Office fédéral de la statistique (2020). [*Méthodes pour les scénarios cantonaux*](https://github.com/statistik-aargau/propop-additional-resources/blob/358ffa280f3777af34d3ac4b2782c1171ed93beb/FSO_2020_Meth_scenarios%20cant.pdf)
:::

```{r}
  # Define nodes

  B [label = < Uses <i>purrr::reduce() </i> to iterate across <BR/> <b> spatial units </b> ,<b> scenarios </b> and <b>years </b> in parameters and population <BR/>and to bind results of year t and year t + 1>, color = 'transparent']
  C [label = < <b> year t </b><BR/>start year or projected year>, fontcolor = '#007AB8']
  D [label = < <b> project_population() </b><BR/>wrapper function>, fontcolor = '#ffa81f']
  E [label = < <b> 1. advance_population() </b><BR/>population ages by one year>, fillcolor = 'transparent']
  F [label = < <b> 2. calculate_projection() </b><BR/>cohort transition;<BR/> aggregates population 100+>, fillcolor = 'transparent']
  G [label = < <b> 3. calculate_newborns() </b><BR/>calculates births>, fillcolor = 'transparent']
  H [label = < <b> results for year t + 1 </b>>, fontcolor = '#007AB8']

  # Align side by side
{ rank=same; A }
{ rank=same; C; D}

  # Define edges (connections)
  A -> B
  B -> C
  C -> D
  D -> E
  E -> F
  F -> G
  G -> H
  H -> C
}
")

graph
```

# First projection

## Exercise 1: run a quick example

Run this example, then inspect the result with `str()` and `View()`.

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: true
library(propop)

projection_canton_2030 <- propop(
  parameters = fso_parameters,
  year_first = 2026,
  year_last = 2030,
  population = fso_population
)
```
\
[**Check:** Do you recognize all components from the equation in the output?]{style="color: #007AB8;"}\

# Input data and function arguments

## What does `propop()` need?

-   A **starting population** (FSO or your own data).
-   **Mandatory input:** birth, mortality and migration rates for each scenario.
\
<span style="color: #007AB8; font-size: 30px;">{{< fa arrow-right >}}</span> see Vignette ["Prepare data"](https://statistik-aargau.github.io/propop/articles/prepare_data.html)
\
-   *Optional: Regionalization and subregional migration*
\
<span style="color: #007AB8; font-size: 30px;">{{< fa arrow-right >}}</span> see Vignette ["Projections for subregions"](https://statistik-aargau.github.io/propop/articles/project_subregions.html).

## Function arguments

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="45%" style="font-size: 110%;"}
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
propop <- function(
    parameters,
    population,
    year_first,
    year_last,
    subregional = FALSE,
    binational = TRUE,
    scenarios = NULL,
    age_groups = 101,
    fert_first = 16,
    fert_last = 50,
    share_born_female = 100 / 205,
    spatial_unit = "Aargau"
)
```
:::

::: {.column width="55%" style="font-size: 75%;"}
**Mandatory:**\
population, parameters, projection period\
\
**Main options**\
-   subregional migration flows (default: no)\
-   one or two nationalities (default: two)\
-   `scenarios`: `NULL` = all scenarios in `parameters`\
\
**Further defaults**\
-   `fert_first`:`fert_last`: fertile period 16 to 50\
-   `share_born_female`: 100/205 = 0.488\
-   `spatial_unit`: name of the region(s)
:::

::::

::: {style="font-size: 95%;"}
Learn more\
<span style="color: #007AB8; font-size: 30px;">{{< fa arrow-right >}}</span> Vignette ["Projections for a single region"](https://statistik-aargau.github.io/propop/articles/project_single_region.html)\
<span style="color: #007AB8; font-size: 30px;">{{< fa arrow-right >}}</span> [`propop::propop()` function documentation](https://github.com/statistik-aargau/propop/blob/main/R/propop.R).
:::

# Coffee break {data-background-color="#004774"}

## Subregional migration and regionalization of components

FSO parameters exist for cantons and Switzerland only. For districts or municipalities or other spatial units, **you need to prepare the parameters**.


## Subregional migration

-   `propop()` can account for migration **between** subregions using:
    -   **rates** for emi- and immigration (`subregional = "rate"`).
    -   **net numbers** for migration (`subregional = "net"`).
\
\

<span style="color: #007AB8; font-size: 30px;">{{< fa arrow-right >}}</span> see Vignette chapter: ["Migration between subregions"](https://statistik-aargau.github.io/propop/articles/project_subregions.html#between-subregions)

## Regionalization of components

::: {style="font-size: 95%;"}
-   In `propop`, you find functions and examples for breaking down components to subregions according to **population size** or **past migration**.

```{r}
#| echo: false
# Create flowchart
graph <- DiagrammeR::grViz("digraph {
graph [layout = dot, rankdir = LR]
node [shape = rectangle, style = \"filled,rounded\", fillcolor = deepskyblue, fontname = Helvetica]
data1 [label = 'Aggregated\npast migration', shape = folder, fillcolor = gold]
calc_emi [label =  'calculate\n_rates']
data2 [label = 'emi_rate\n= emigration\nrate\n per group', shape = folder, fillcolor = gold]
calc_hist [label =  'calculate\n_shares']
data3 [label = 'imm_share\n= immigration\n share\nper group', shape = folder, fillcolor = gold]
propop [label =  'propop']
result [label= 'Population\nprojection\nresult', shape = folder, fillcolor = gold]
{data1}  -> calc_emi -> data2 -> propop
{data1}  ->calc_hist -> data3 -> propop -> result
}", height = 200, width = 800)

graph
```

-   Birth rates can be adjusted with the package [`propopbirth`](https://statistik-aargau.github.io/propopbirth/).
-   Custom parameters (e.g. region-specific international immigration) are passed via the `parameters` object.
:::

::: {style="font-size: 95%;"}
<span style="color: #007AB8; font-size: 30px;">{{< fa arrow-right >}}</span> see Vignette chapter: ["Breaking down to subregions"](https://statistik-aargau.github.io/propop/articles/project_subregions.html#breaking-down)
:::

# Evaluate and compare

## Error metrics

::: {style="font-size: 80%;"}
| Metric | What it tells you | Why useful |
|-----------------|--------------------------|-------------------------|
| `pe` (percentage error) | Deviation of projection from benchmark, in % | Shows **direction**: over- or underestimation |
| `ape` (absolute percentage error) | Size of the deviation, ignoring direction | Errors can't cancel out; easy to interpret |
| `w_ape` (weighted APE) | APE weighted by group size | Small groups don't dominate the result |
| `mpe` (aggregated) | Mean of `pe` across all observations | Reveals systematic **bias** |
| `ape_under_5` (aggregated) | Share of observations with small error | Quick quality indicator |
:::

## Weights and grouping

::: {style="font-size: 85%;"}
[**Weights**]{style="color: #007AB8;"}

[{{< fa square-check size=1x title="square-check" >}}]{style="color: #4c8562;"} Small groups tend to have larger errors; weighting corrects for this (example: `ape` 0.39 / 0.36 → `w_ape` 0.24 / 0.07)\
[{{< fa circle-minus size=1x title="minus" >}}]{style="color: #FF82a9;"} Large groups dominate; poor fit in small groups (e.g. very old people) is easily hidden\
[{{< fa circle-minus size=1x title="minus" >}}]{style="color: #FF82a9;"} Results depend on the chosen weighting (`weight_groups`)

\

[**Larger age groups** (e.g. 0-19, 20-64, 65+)]{style="color: #007AB8;"}

[{{< fa square-check size=1x title="square-check" >}}]{style="color: #4c8562;"} Fewer tiny groups, so fewer problems when the benchmark is 0\
[{{< fa square-check size=1x title="square-check" >}}]{style="color: #4c8562;"} More stable, more readable results\
[{{< fa circle-minus size=1x title="minus" >}}]{style="color: #FF82a9;"} Errors can cancel out within a group\
[{{< fa circle-minus size=1x title="minus" >}}]{style="color: #FF82a9;"} Less detail about *where* the model is weak
:::

Compare the projections for your canton to

-   **your own projections**.

::: {.callout-note}
## Steps
1. Prepare your own data or download the data for your canton using the propop-functions `get_population()` and `get_parameters()`.

2. Run the projections.

3. Prepare the evaluation (`prepare_evaluation()`).

4. Calculate error metrics (`compute_measures()` and `aggregate_measures()`).

5. Visualize the differences between models.
:::
:::
:::

# Wrap-up

## Package overview: functions at a glance

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="25%" style="font-size: 65%;"}
[{{< fa database size=2x >}}]{style="color: #007AB8;"}  **1. Get data**

`get_population()`\
Starting population and benchmark from the FSO (PXWeb)

`get_parameters()`\
FSO scenario parameters

*Package data:*\
`fso_population`, `fso_parameters`, `ag_population_subregional`, `ag_migration_subregional`
:::

::: {.column width="25%" style="font-size: 65%;"}
[{{< fa map-location-dot size=2x >}}]{style="color: #007AB8;"}  **2. Regionalize**

`calculate_shares()`\
Shares of the canton-wide number of people per subregion, from past migration (`imm_share`)

`calculate_rates()`\
Mean emigration rate per group and subregion from past migration (`emi_rate`)
:::

::: {.column width="25%" style="font-size: 65%;"}
[{{< fa chart-line size=2x >}}]{style="color: #007AB8;"}  **3. Projection**

`propop()`

-   `scenarios` (e.g. reference, high, low)
-   `binational`: with or without nationality distinction
-   `subregional`:
    -   `FALSE`: single region (default)
    -   `"rate"`: needs `emi_sub`, `imm_sub`
    -   `"net"`: needs `mig_sub`; can produce negative numbers in small groups
:::

::: {.column width="25%" style="font-size: 65%;"}
[{{< fa magnifying-glass-chart size=2x >}}]{style="color: #007AB8;"}  **4. Evaluate**

`prepare_evaluation()`\
Combines benchmark and projection

`compute_measures()`\
Error metrics per observation (`pe`, `ape`, `w_ape`)

`aggregate_measures()`\
Summary metrics across observations
:::
